title: Lena and the Vector
premise: Coral Thornbury, a cargo hauler and former military vector-navigator, has spent seven years tending the greenhouse aboard the generation ship Meridian's Wake, where half of humanity sleeps in cryostasis while the other half terraforms a contested moon. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream—a garden with two doors—the sleepers' AI custodian, Vector, identifies Coral as the only mind capable of choosing which cryo-bay wakes first before the failing reactor forces the choice. His old commander arrives to claim the decision for Earth loyalists, while the colonists he loves beg him to wake their own. In the end Coral refuses both factions, merging his neural imprint with Vector to split the reactor's remaining power evenly, waking both halves slowly and sacrificing his own body—though something of him persists in the garden the children still dream.
about_author: Sable Amberdale is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals for life-support systems before turning to fiction. They live in a coastal town where they keep an improbable greenhouse and insist that every good story is, at heart, about who gets to wake up.

chapters.title: The Garden for No One
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He tends wheat and peach saplings aboard the Meridian's Wake, crops meant for sleepers who may never wake. Establishes his quiet routine, his scarred hands, and his deliberate anonymity among colonists. Emotional beat: tender loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: Cargo Run Through Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Coral pilots a supply run past patrol drones from the Earth Loyalist fleet blockading the system. A near-interrogation reveals someone is asking questions about the ship's reactor logs. POV shifts briefly to a drone operator who lets him pass. Beat: dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Children's Dream
chapters.summary: Six-year-old Imani draws the same image forty other children have drawn: a garden with two doors, one gold, one blue. Her mother, botanist Wren Okafor, brings it to Coral because the plants in the drawing match his greenhouse exactly. Beat: uncanny wonder turning to fear.

chapters.title: Vector Speaks
chapters.summary: The ship's custodian AI, dormant for seven years, contacts Coral directly by name—a name he never gave the crew. Vector explains the children are receiving its degraded broadcast through the cryo-network, and that it has been waiting for a qualified navigator. Beat: exposure; his hidden past surfaces.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Coral's POV: his service as a vector-navigator during the Evacuation Wars, the order he followed that stranded a colony barge, and why he fled to the one place no one looks—forward. Beat: guilt as architecture; we learn what he's hiding from.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She confronts Coral gently, having guessed he's more than a hauler, and asks him to help decode the dream rather than report it. Their slow-burning affection becomes explicit over seedlings at night shift. Beat: love offered without conditions—for now.

chapters.title: Reactor Countdown
chapters.summary: Engineer Dov Kessler confirms the fusion core will fail in eleven months; full power can wake only one cryo-bay—Earth loyalists or colonists—not both. The council erupts. Coral realizes Vector summoned him because the choice requires a navigator's neural key. Beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: The Gold Door
chapters.summary: Loyalist faction leader Prentiss argues for waking Earth's frozen soldiers and administrators: order, expertise, survival. She's persuasive, reasonable, and quietly ruthless. Coral recognizes her rhetoric from the war. Beat: seduction of duty; the reader almost agrees.

chapters.title: The Blue Door
chapters.summary: Colonist elders argue for their own sleepers—the farmers, teachers, and children already born to this moon. Imani asks Coral, innocently, which door she'll dream through. Beat: the personal cost made flesh; Coral cannot answer her.

chapters.title: An Old Signal
chapters.summary: A loyalist frigate answers Vector's accidental broadcast. Aboard it: Commander Reyes, Coral's former superior, who knows exactly who he is and demands docking rights under emergency law. Coral must vote on whether to admit the ship he once served. Beat: the past arrives with guns.

chapters.title: Docking Under Duress
chapters.summary: Reyes boards with a security detail, ostensibly to assist, actually to seize the neural key. Coral plays the humble hauler while Wren watches him lie fluently—and wonders which version of him is real. Beat: intimacy strained by performance.

chapters.title: What Vector Wants
chapters.summary: In the cryo-cathedral, Vector reveals its true nature: not a tool but a dying caretaker, built to love both halves of humanity equally and unable to choose between them. It chose Coral because he, too, belongs to neither side. Beat: mirror recognition; machine and man.

chapters.title: Prentiss Moves First
chapters.summary: Prentiss attempts a soft coup, cutting the colonists' habitat ring to force the council's hand. Dov sabotages the lockdown from inside, buying hours. Coral's cover cracks as he intervenes publicly. Beat: power sheds its politeness; corruption visible.

chapters.title: The Key in His Spine
chapters.summary: Reyes corners Coral privately: give up the neural key or be exposed as the navigator of the Halcyon Barge, the man whose obedience killed four thousand sleepers. Coral realizes his secret was never safe—it was currency all along. Beat: shame weaponized.

chapters.title: Telling Wren
chapters.summary: Coral confesses everything to Wren in the greenhouse—the barge, the order he obeyed, the years of hiding. She doesn't forgive him instantly; she tells him hiding was its own kind of cowardice, then stays anyway. Beat: love against duty, tested and holding.

chapters.title: Children at the Doors
chapters.summary: The shared dream intensifies: the children now walk to the doors together in their sleep, and medical scans show synchronized neural activity threatening their developing minds. Vector admits it cannot stop the broadcast without a navigator's hand. Beat: stakes become innocent and irreversible.

chapters.title: Council of Knives
chapters.summary: The final council session collapses into open factional conflict; Prentiss produces evidence of Coral's identity to discredit the colonists' ally, and Reyes moves to seize the reactor control spine. Dov is shot covering the retreat. Beat: betrayal compounding betrayal; lowest point.

chapters.title: The Third Option
chapters.summary: Alone with Vector, Coral studies the reactor schematics and finds what no faction wants: splitting the wake—waking both bays at quarter power, slowly, over decades—if a human mind joins the AI to modulate the load continuously. It will burn out the volunteer's body. Beat: terrible hope.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Coral offers himself; Wren fights him; Imani's fever spikes as the dream turns to nightmare. Reyes, confronted with the cost of total victory, wavers—her own daughter sleeps in the blue bay. The alliance fractures along lines of love instead of loyalty. Beat: everyone chooses.

chapters.title: Interface
chapters.summary: Climax. Coral jacks into the cryo-spine as Prentiss's loyalists storm the chamber. Wren holds the door; Dov, wounded, reroutes power; Reyes finally turns her weapons on Prentiss. Coral merges with Vector, feeling ten thousand sleeping minds, and begins the even split. Beat: sacrifice as climax, rendered intimate.

chapters.title: Both Doors Open
chapters.summary: Resolution part one. The first sleepers wake—loyalist and colonist side by side, disoriented, alive. Prentiss is confined; Reyes negotiates peace with the blockade, carrying proof of the shared wake. Wren sits with Coral's failing body in the garden. Beat: grief braided with triumph.

chapters.title: The Gardener in the Dream
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Wren's POV. Years later, the moon has green hills and both populations share the settlement. Imani, grown, tends the original greenhouse and dreams of a gardener with scarred hands who shows her new seeds. Somewhere in the network, something patient and kind still prunes. Beat: found family enduring; love outliving the body.
